description: Open wins: measurable open problems in Guarana that a contributor can take, with the scene, today's number, the target, where in the code to look and where to discuss it. Read by site/wins.html. Edit by hand when a number moves or a win is taken; move a finished win to status "won" and keep it, with the pull request.
reward: Your name in the release notes, the hall of fame and the app's credits.
how_to_claim: Comment on the issue with what you will try, then open a pull request that shows the number moving on the scene, with the baseline next to it (AGENTS.md, rule 1). A fix that does not move the number is still welcome as a measurement.

wins.title: Read-back stalls: the guest waits on GPU read-backs
wins.scene: A profiled gameplay scene on the maintainer's Intel Arc 140T laptop (EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=1 logs 'Async read-back per second').

target.text: 33.6 ms or better with the switch off, the figure EDEN_NX2_EARLY_AFTER=1 already reaches in the same scene

files: src/video_core (the GPU back thread and its queue)
wins.next_step: A read path for the guest that does not wait behind the GPU back thread's queue.
wins.measure: python -I tools/nx2/debug_mcp.py --server 127.0.0.1:6545 --call '{"method":"frame_times","params":{"seconds":10}}' with EDEN_NX2_GPU_PROFILE=1, baseline and change back to back.

wins.title: First-visit shader stutter
wins.scene: Any scene the first time it is visited, with a cleared pipeline cache (EDEN_NX2_STUTTER_TRACE=1 names each frame over 33 ms and its cause).
wins.metric: Frames over 33 ms caused by a pipeline built on the GPU thread, first visit

current.text: Not yet counted on a fixed scene: the first measured count is a win of its own

target.text: None on the first visit of the scene

wins.next_step: Graphics pipeline library fast-link (VK_EXT_graphics_pipeline_library): the Intel Arc driver exposes it, so a draw can use a fast-linked pipeline while the optimized one builds.
wins.measure: Nx2StutterSummary in the log (frame-time histogram and builds), python -I tools/nx2/cache_metrics.py compare for A/B runs.

wins.title: Boot time: the Vulkan instance takes seconds
wins.scene: Cold start of the emulator to the first frame of any game (Nx2Boot lines with EDEN_NX2_STUTTER_TRACE=1).

target.text: Under 1 s (proposed; the first measured gain sets the real bar)

wins.next_step: Find out whether the Intel driver's shader cache size is what the instance waits for, then avoid it or defer it.
wins.measure: The Nx2Boot phases in the log, cold and warm, with python -I tools/nx2/cache_bench.py or by hand.

wins.title: Hyrule Field: a steady 30 fps
wins.scene: Ocarina of Time, Hyrule Field (the tools/bench scene oot-hyrule-field), Intel Arc 140T.

target.text: A steady 30 fps, p99 frame time included

files: src/core (the guest threads and the JIT)
wins.next_step: Find what the guest's main thread spends its frame on: EDEN_NX2_GUEST_THREAD_STATS=1 splits it into game code, SVCs and waits.
wins.measure: python -I tools/bench/bench.py run on the oot-hyrule-field scene; only rows that are valid with scene_ok true count.

wins.title: AMD Radeon 780M and 890M: the first reports
wins.scene: Ocarina of Time, Hyrule Field, with tools/bench on a Radeon 780M or 890M machine (a handheld or a laptop).

current.text: 0 verified-scene reports for AMD Radeon 780M / 760M or 880M / 890M

wins.next_step: Run the scene and send the device report; set 'Credit me as' to your GitHub handle to be named on the Records board.

wins.title: Controller gyro and rumble: a pass over real pads
wins.scene: A game that uses motion and vibration, with a pad that has both (DualSense, Switch Pro, Joy-Con), on any GPU.
wins.metric: Pads where gyro and rumble both work

target.text: A written pass per pad family: what works, what does not, and the fix for what does not

wins.next_step: Test each pad family, write down what fails, then fix the first thing that fails.
wins.measure: Pass or fail per pad, game and feature, with the pad's model and connection (USB or Bluetooth).
